content: 1. Methylene blue has the potential to increase serotonin levels due to its inhibition of monoamine oxidase A (MAO-A). If administration of methylene blue is necessary, serotonergic drugs should be discontinued immediately, and the patient should be closely monitored for signs of central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Serotonergic therapy can be resumed either 24 hours after the last dose of methylene blue or after two weeks of monitoring, whichever occurs first. 2. Hyoscyamine and trospium chloride both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended when these agents are used together. 3. Umeclidinium bromide and hyoscyamine both decrease cholinergic effects and transmission. Use these drugs with caution and monitor the patient closely. If possible, avoid the concurrent use of additional anticholinergic agents. 4. The combination of hyoscyamine and umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled may result in increased toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. Concomitant use of other anticholinergic-containing drugs may lead to additive anticholinergic adverse effects. 5. Co-administration of valbenazine with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), such as methylene blue, may increase monoamine neurotransmitter concentrations in synapses, potentially raising the risk of serotonin syndrome or diminishing the therapeutic effect of valbenazine. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor the patient closely. 6. Hyoscyamine and vecuronium both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Use caution and monitor the patient closely when these agents are used together. 7. Methylene blue and venlafaxine both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If methylene blue must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. Serotonergic therapy may be resumed 24 hours after the last dose of methylene blue or after two weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 8. Methylene blue and vilazodone both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If methylene blue must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. Serotonergic therapy may be resumed 24 hours after the last dose of methylene blue or after two weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 9. Methylene blue increases the toxicity of vortioxetine by elevating serotonin levels. This combination is contraindicated. If methylene blue must be urgently administered, discontinue vortioxetine immediately and monitor for serotonin syndrome. Monitor for serotonin syndrome for three weeks or 24 hours after the last dose of methylene blue, whichever comes first. Vortioxetine may be resumed 24 hours after the last dose of methylene blue. 10. Hyoscyamine decreases the levels of ziprasidone by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, hyoscyamine decreases ziprasidone levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while ziprasidone increases the effects of hyoscyamine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Additive anticholinergic effects and potential hypoglycemia may occur. 11. Zolmitriptan and methylene blue both increase serotonin levels. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If methylene blue must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for CNS toxicity. Serotonergic therapy may be resumed 24 hours after the last dose of methylene blue or after two weeks of monitoring, whichever comes first. 12. Hyoscyamine decreases the levels of zotepine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Hyoscyamine also decreases zotepine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 13. Cardiovascular side effects may include flushing. Central nervous system side effects may include dizziness and drowsiness. Genitourinary side effects may include difficulty urinating and acute urinary retention. Gastrointestinal side effects may include dry mouth. Respiratory side effects may include shortness of breath or difficulty breathing. Anaphylactic reactions, such as itching, rash, severe dizziness, swelling, or trouble breathing, may occur. Hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients is possible. 14. Use caution in patients with a history of intolerance to salicylates or belladonna alkaloids. Do not exceed the recommended dosage, and discontinue use immediately if tachycardia, blurred vision, or other adverse effects occur. Delayed gastric emptying may complicate the management of gastric ulcers. Hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients is possible; carefully weigh the risks and benefits in patients with cardiac disease, especially those with arrhythmias, congestive heart failure, coronary heart disease, or mitral stenosis. 15. Use caution in patients with gastrointestinal tract obstructive disease, glaucoma, or myasthenia gravis. Acute urinary retention may be precipitated in patients with obstructive uropathy, such as bladder neck obstruction due to prostatic hypertrophy. 16. Reproductive studies have not been conducted with this drug combination. Methenamine and hyoscyamine are known to cross the placenta. It is not known whether this drug combination causes fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman or if it affects reproductive capacity. Administer therapy to a pregnant woman only if clearly needed. 17. Problems in humans have not been documented. Methenamine and traces of hyoscyamine are excreted in breast milk. Administer therapy to a nursing mother with caution and only if clearly needed. 18. Methylene blue possesses weak antiseptic properties. It is well absorbed by the gastrointestinal tract and rapidly reduced to leukomethylene blue, which is stabilized in some combination form in the urine. Approximately 75% is excreted unchanged. 19. Phenyl salicylate releases salicylate, which acts as a mild analgesic for pain. Sodium phosphate monobasic is an acidifier that helps maintain an acidic pH in the urine, which is necessary for the degradation of methenamine. 20. Pharmacokinetic parameters described are for each agent administered as monotherapy. These values may differ when administered in combination, but such data have not been provided by the manufacturer. 21.
